text:
tomas: FYI CI perf alert this morning on master, decode short-seq p95 jumped ~15-20% after last night's merges.

maya: oh no. which jobs triggered? link?

ryan: saw the alert too. decode-shortseq canary (perf-ci) — baseline p95 ~46ms -> now ~54ms. tail heavier than before.

tomas: suspect PR #11234 (scheduler: prefer-high-throughput tie-break) + a tiny kv-evict tweak. starting a bisect but initial sampling points at the scheduler change.

maya: reproduced locally with shortseq (len~32). profiler shows increased kernel_switch events per token.

perf-bot: flamegraph: s3://perf-artifacts/3456723456/flame.svg — decode path has ~20% more time in kernel-switch overhead.

ryan: logs:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:01Z] batch_size=4 -> chosen_kernel=attn_fuse_v2
[2026-03-18T03:12:01Z] batch_size=5 -> chosen_kernel=attn_generic
[2026-03-18T03:12:01Z] kernel_switch_cost=3.9ms
```

maya: the scheduler tie-breaker nudged several batches from 4->5 which crosses the kernel-selector boundary; for short sequences the generic kernel increases per-token latency despite higher throughput for long seqs.

jen: emergent interaction between scheduler heuristics and kernel selector thresholds. short-term: do we revert the scheduler change or adjust selector thresholds?

tomas: prefer minimal-risk hotfix: bump selector threshold conservatively so shortseq stays on fuse kernel. hold rollout until we validate.

ryan: wrote a small reproducer: `scripts/repro_shortseq.sh --seed 7 --iters 1000` — artifacts uploaded to perf bucket. Repro shows pre-merge p95 46.3ms, post-merge 54.8ms.

maya: quick experiment bumping selector threshold 0.58->0.72 dropped kernel_switch_count and restored p95 to ~47.2ms. patch small but needs canary.

jen: alternative is making scheduler avoid promoting batches across that boundary for short sequences, but that's more invasive.

tomas: open hotfix PR for selector threshold change + unit/regression test (eng-runtime#11890). also add metric kernel_switch_count per request so we can detect regressions earlier.

perf-bot: hotfix CI (job 7893) artifacts: p95=47.5ms, kernel_switch_count median back to 0-1.

release-bot: Rollout paused: blocking perf regression on master.

ryan: if hotfix passes canary we resume. if not, plan B is reverting PR#11234 (revert PR#11892) and re-bisecting.

maya: adding a shortseq-focused unit test that asserts kernel_switch_count <=1 for seq_len<=40; pushed to tomas/hf-kernel-threshold branch.

tomas: updating incident tracker and runbook note: diagnostic checklist = 1) batch-size distribution, 2) kernel selection histogram, 3) kernel_switch_count, 4) flamegraph.

jen: :thumbsup: good plan.

ryan: hotfix canary passed, unpausing rollout. keeping extra canary monitoring window for 2h. will close thread if stable.

perf-bot: last_message: canary window started, monitoring metrics streaming to dashboard (dashboards/perf/decode_shortseq).

maya: follow-up action: docs + small design note on scheduler-selector interaction so future heuristics consider kernel boundaries.

tomas: thanks everyone — closing once monitoring window completes.
